body: Current GCC opportunity census: a correct 1024-element unsigned array update/reduction loop executes100000 rounds. Native FAST runtime median **227.10ms**, GCC O0 **103.42ms**, O2 **37.80ms**. Median matched O2/Buster0.16674 => GCC **6.00x faster**, wins12/12, disjoint ranges. Text **580/307/359B** (B/G0/G2). Independent Python modulo-2^32 expected output and every runtime transcript agree. O2 disassembly uses SSE2 packed initialization, updates and reduction; native FAST is scalar with repeated address/phi stack traffic. This supports a bounded vectorization/scalar-loop census, not a claim that SLP alone or a512-bit vocabulary will recover6x. Source is retained in artifact as array_loop.c; vectors and scalar/edge improvements need separate ablations. No competing implementation claim. Evidence: Buster d4ca72fb4e97ae0a410b0d03258b00495fa45e13, trusted Clang21.1.8 Release; Ubuntu GCC15.2.0-16ubuntu1; hosted EPYC7763. Corrected [run37005475203](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/37005475203), diagnostic branch e19b531e03db62afd8f688ecd69d7f9f111283bf, artifact SHA256 `47c04b2c3f12e26c1346c4dbde0face10643dbc7a0256e364495a5686fec94ec` independently verified. Explicit baseline ISA, non-PIC/non-PIE, same GNU11/wrapv/alias/char semantics, common GCC CRT/linker,12 matched rounds/all six orders, all output/hash oracles passed. Stock GCC distro hardening retained; no isolated hardening/pass ablation. This is diagnostic, not Zen5/native-retirement acceptance.
